query: evidence that older methods for Publish the stage-2 inlier-face width, height, and depth in metres on /pps/pallet_pose_rich with the pose from that same estimate. Width is the camera-x span of the inlier face, height is the camera-y span, and depth is the mean range. The vehicle's dynamic handling process can then size the pallet from the pose it is about to use while the scene can still change. have been superseded
findings: A stored pallet size is the older size. Zhao et al., Appl. Sci. 2022, 12(20):10331, say one shape feature cannot represent pallets because apparent shape and size change with angle, yet their labeled template still stores pallet dimensions and rescales it from a distance statistic. Wu et al., Sensors 2025, 25(7):2333, say the later RGB-D front-face and point-cloud slot method still needs those prior features and dimensions, and it errs when the approach angle is arbitrary or the pallet type changes. LiDAR slot finding fails the same way when hole sizes differ. Wu's replacement segments the stringer and slots on the current view, without a stored size, because a hybrid warehouse must react while people or vehicles can still appear.

That known-size pose solve has not been fully retired. Mueller et al., arXiv:2503.22965, still require known Euro faces, 1200x144 mm or 800x144 mm, before PnP. Miura et al., VISAPP 2026, still use 1100x150x1100 mm and say NOCS-style and FoundationPose methods at about 1-4 FPS are hard to run on a forklift. Nguyen et al., arXiv:2508.15427, still pass a pallet CAD model into FoundationPose. Known size is superseded when the type or angle is not the stored one, not in every real-time forklift pipeline.

Camera-x and camera-y spans (max minus min of the face points) are the older axis-aligned size. With a pose, the size that belongs on that message is the full side length along the pose axes. vision_msgs BoundingBox3D, issue 101, defines size that way. Yu et al., arXiv:2507.00984 (1 Jul 2025), estimate T in SE(3) and S = (width, height, depth) together, as a scaled unit cube, from the same stereo keypoints. A yawed face's camera-x span is the projected extent and is larger than the face width. SICK US10262222 rotates the cluster until the ground is z=0, then measures the enclosing rectangle.

Mean range of the raw face is the older depth, and object-frame (short, long, height) is not always the successor. Völk et al., arXiv:2308.06306, predict a front-face distance separately from the box dimensions, and they say camera-view (width, depth, height) is easier to learn than (short, long, height) when the rotation may be wrong, because a bad depth dimension makes the object-frame size fail. Camera-frame extents therefore remain the fallback when orientation is uncertain. What those pipelines drop is the mean of an unaligned cluster: the depth they publish is the front-face distance, or the translation of the same pose.
